boundaries: MappingResolverImpl/fork Fabric Loader implementation and actual mapping bytes
FART Renamer/EnhancedRemapper scheduling, extra-entry processing, inheritance lookup and serialization behavior
Adapter Patch DSL, dynamic algorithms, BFU, generated-class map implementation and actual patch_data.json/lvt_offsets.json
Forge/ModLauncher/CoreModProvider internals and real Forge-patched Minecraft class shape
Mixin fork private fields, class provider and runtime injector matching
Actual Fabric mod jars, mixin/refmap/AW bytes and client/server runtime combinations
verification: Required scope inventory equals on-disk transformer/** and coremod resource inventory
Every included SHA256 equals anchor inventory and preexisting CAS content hash
All public source references pinned to the exact ANCHOR revision
No builds, runtime, installation or publication performed

findings.summary: The explicit normal builder order is signature, field/accessor/reflection, namespace, helper callsites, Mixin/class patches, refmap/manifest, metadata, optional AW conversion.
All-current inputs skip transform-batch initialization and generated Adapter output regeneration.
Generated metadata library branch copies the jar and adds only absent pack metadata.
Non-intermediary declared namespace logs an error but continues with intermediary mapping logic.
An exact armor ModifyArg selector changes target overload, Model parameter/return types, casts and instanceof/early-return control flow.
Inline annotation remapping is selected by declared refmap-name emptiness, so declared-but-missing files do not automatically activate it.
Original presence of an AT suppresses the separate AW-to-AT transformer.
Explicit key is implementation-version plus physical dist plus optional input SHA; output filename adds naming and Minecraft version, while dependency changes are not independently fingerprinted.
Coremod-bytecode errors log and return original class bytes while metadata lookup delegates upstream.

cross_callsite_review_note.observation: Standard fabricloader constraints are removed unless an earlier configured alias branch handles them. With only removed standard constraints, getMixinCompat uses default 0.10.0; surviving fabric-loader or alias-produced constraints can enter interval branches.
